advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `"indeterminate": []` to `_empty_binding_drift()` (and use plain append) so the bucket is always present like every other drift class.
evidence: Test asserts conditional presence: `assert "indeterminate" not in live` and `assert "indeterminate" not in done` (tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_fsck_keyset_prev_heldout.py)
advisory.finding: The new `indeterminate` drift bucket is not initialized in `_empty_binding_drift()` and is populated via `drift.setdefault("indeterminate", [])`, so unlike every other drift class the key is only present when non-empty. A consumer indexing `drift["indeterminate"]` directly (rather than `.get`) will KeyError on the common empty case; the test suite itself relies on this by asserting `"indeterminate" not in live`.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `"indeterminate": []` to the dict returned by `_empty_binding_drift()` and replace `drift.setdefault("indeterminate", []).append(...)` with `drift["indeterminate"].append(...)`; update tests that assert absence to assert `== []`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Broaden the fence to fire whenever a TERMINAL local's present Jira entry carries no usable status (e.g. `not _jira_status(jira_fields)`), not only exact `{}`.
advisory.finding: The key-set fence triggers only on the exact literal `jira_fields == {}`. A key-set entry stored as `None`, or any present entry whose status is empty/None (e.g. `{"status": None}` or `{"status": ""}`), bypasses the fence and falls through to `classify()`, where `_jira_status` returns `""` (not in `_JIRA_TERMINAL_STATUSES`) and a TERMINAL local yields a false `would_terminal` — the very false-drift this change intends to prevent.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace `jira_fields == {}` with a status-presence check such as `not classify_mod._jira_status(jira_fields)` (or an equivalent public helper), so any status-less present entry for a terminal local is treated as indeterminate.

coaching.coaching: File a follow-on ticket (discovered_from this change) for brittleness of exact empty-dict fence condition, a pre-existing / out-of-scope issue — do not fix it in this change.
coaching.subject: brittleness of exact empty-dict fence condition
